newsitem.title: UK: UK minister welcomes banks' small firms code.
newsitem.headline: UK minister welcomes banks' small firms code.

text.p: A government minister on Wednesday welcomed the publication by the British Bankers' Association of a new code for their relations with small business customers, but said he would be watching closely to see it was honoured.

The Trade and Industry Department said that under the new code, banks had agreed to provide such customers with early warning of any concerns they have, to support businesses in difficulty where feasible, and to encourage better communications.

"This is a very positive step forward and will bring about a very useful shift in the way banks and businesses operate. It must be better for all concerned," Competition and Consumer Affairs Minister Nigel Griffiths said.
But he added: "I will be watching the banks closely to see that they are implementing the code properly. If they are not, I will want explanations from them."
Fifteen major banks, who hold the accounts of some 97 percent of Britain's small- and medium-sized enterprises, have agreed to operate the code.
